title: Yellow Fever – Kenya, WHO Disease Outbreak News 361 (vaccination status, certificate validity, bite avoidance)
claims: Kenyan national authorities require yellow fever vaccination for international travellers over one year of age entering Kenya; WHO recommends vaccination for travellers aged 9 months or over, except those whose itinerary is limited to listed low-risk areas (including Nairobi and Mombasa cities).

Under the International Health Regulations (2005), the International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis becomes valid 10 days after vaccination and remains valid for the vaccinated person's lifetime; a single approved dose gives lifelong protection and no booster is required as an entry condition.

WHO general precaution is avoidance of mosquito bites, including repellents and insecticide-treated nets; yellow fever virus transmission risk is highest during the day and early evening; travellers should seek medical advice rapidly if symptoms suggestive of infection appear.
